transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-01-10 15:00 UTC
Duration: 1:12
Attendees: Lina Ortega (Redwood AE), Marcus Chen (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Redwood Partner Ops); Dave Hersch (StratusWorks VP Sales), Meera Patel (StratusWorks GTN Lead), Tom Novak (StratusWorks Solutions Architect), Aisha Rahman (StratusWorks Channel Ops)

Summary: quick partner co-sell sync to align on top target accounts, define who owns which stages, confirm the tech benchmark approach for Dedicated infra, and agree go/no-go gating for Q1 joint outreach.

Topics: account mapping, referral/commission tiers, technical benchmark scope (latency/cost/throughput), compliance checks (SOC2/VPC/KMS), marketplace listing timing, joint demo cadence.

Transcript:
[00:00] Lina Ortega: hey everyone, thanks for carving out time. I think we have about, what, 70 minutes? trying to be respectful of people end of week load — we wanted to run through the joint account list and the high-level playbook and then Marcus will go into the benchmark ask, ok?
[00:18] Dave Hersch: yep, sounds good. we've got a couple AEs on the call who are in backchannel but not in this bridge, so if we need to loop them we'll do that. main thing for us: predictability on capacity and clear lead routing, we can't have leads fall off.
[00:30] Marcus Chen: cool. quick note, when we say "Dedicated" some folks transcribe it as "Readwood Dedi" in notes — so if we say Redwood Dedicated, that's the reserved GPU pool option, predictable latency and throughput.
[00:40] Meera Patel: yes, latency vs cost is the conversation. for our mid-market book we need low cost per token, for our strategic accounts we care about latency and SLOs. how are we thinking about routing?
[00:50] Priya Nair: partner ops perspective — we want clarity on who owns discovery → demo → contract. our ideal is to have StratusWorks own initial contact, Redwood steps in for technical validation and benchmark, then joint commercial. commission tiers need to be defined.
[01:05] Tom Novak: technical question up front: will the benchmark require us to send data into Redwood hosted environment or can we run the same tests in a VPC/private bundle? some of our customers are very strict on data residency.
[01:18] Marcus Chen: good call — we can do both. for quick early-stage demo use hosted API, but for any regulated use or enterprise POC we'll spin up a Redwood Private (VPC) instance or Dedicated pool in your cloud region. for the benchmark we'll propose two tracks: hosted sandbox for speed, and a private Dedicated run for the top 3 accounts.
[01:34] Aisha Rahman: also need to confirm SSO + SCIM — our field wants single-sign on for demo environments so SEs can jump in. is that standard?
[01:42] Lina Ortega: yes we support SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning; we'll share our SSO instructions and the SCIM endpoint details. and yes we have SOC2 Type II — Marcus will attach the security pack in the follow-up.
[01:52] Dave Hersch: great. on commission models, what's typical? flat referral vs tiered?
[01:58] Priya Nair: from Redwood partner ops, common is a revenue-split or referral % for first-year ARR. we'll propose a tiered referral e.g., 8% for up to $250k ARR, 5% after. but we want StratusWorks input because some deals will be net-new vs co-sell.
[02:12] Meera Patel: can we get a sample invoice / commission flow? procurement wants clarity on who issues credits on deals with marketplace listings.
[02:21] Lina Ortega: yes, we'll draft a 1-pager on billing/marketplace flows and include examples.
[02:26] Marcus Chen: ok jumping into the bench plan — for the Dedicated run we want to measure cold-start latency, 95th percentile token latency at target concurrency, and cost per 1k tokens with our batching profile. recommended test matrix attached in notes (we'll send).
[02:42] Tom Novak: what's the expected hardware for Dedicated in the benchmark? A100? H100?
[02:47] Marcus Chen: depends on target model — for 70B-ish models we usually recommend H100 or a quantized A100 stack for cost testing. we'll include H100 + 80-bit (?) hmm — that was my mouth, but more likely H100 and q8-bit paths for cost. some transcriber stuff might call it "q ate" — sorry that's transcription noise.
[03:06] Meera Patel: ok that level's helpful. how long will a Dedicated run take to set up? we need to plan se calendar.
[03:12] Marcus Chen: provision time is ~48–72 hours once we have infra ok and the account mapping. if you want private on-prem, that adds lead time and an Ops window.
[03:21] Dave Hersch: for go-to-market, we want a joint blitz on top 25 accounts. Meera's team will own account outreach, Redwood to provide co-branded deck + tech SE for demos.
[03:31] Priya Nair: can we talk leads attribution? we prefer first-touch credit to StratusWorks for co-sell sourced leads, but joint net-new plays need a split. we'll propose an attribution matrix.
[03:42] Lina Ortega: quick interjection—we also have the "smart routing" feature where requests can be routed by policy (latency, cost, region). that helps when StratusWorks wants certain accounts on Dedicated so traffic automatically goes to the reserved pool.
[03:55] Tom Novak: that's useful; does that require any SDK changes on your side?
[03:59] Marcus Chen: not SDK changes, it's config and route policy. we can provide a JSON policy sample. also, caching/prefix KV cache can reduce token cost for repeated prompts which matters for demo scripts.
[04:12] Meera Patel: perfect. can we also get an example of per-route cost breakdown so sales can model TCO for customers?
[04:18] Lina Ortega: yes, Redwood Console exposes token-level cost and latency — we'll export a sample per-route CSV for your finance models.
[04:24] Dave Hersch: security: KMS integration — do you support customer-managed keys? some of our finance customers insist on HSM-backed keys.
[04:31] Marcus Chen: yep, we support KMS/HSM integrations for Private deployments; for Hosted we have envelope encryption and we can bring-your-own-key for enterprise tiers. we'll put that in the security doc.
[04:41] Meera Patel: ok. marketplace listing: how long from joint agreement to listing? we have an internal timeline tied to our FY kickoff.
[04:47] Priya Nair: marketplace cadence typically 3–6 weeks from contract signature, depending on legal/compliance checks. we can fast-track if both legal teams sync.
[04:55] Aisha Rahman: quick nit — we saw a competitor (Anthropic) run a co-sell promo recently; how do we differentiate?
[04:59] Lina Ortega: we focus on production economics and predictable inference. messaging: unified inference across hosted/dedicated/private, cost controls (batching/quantization recommendations), and reliability with graceful fallbacks. we'll share a competitive playbook excerpt.
[05:14] Dave Hersch: sounds good. operationally, who is the contact for escalations? we need one POC per org.
[05:20] Priya Nair: Priya will be Redwood's partner ops POC for commercial, Marcus for technical, Lina for AE coordination. StratusWorks to confirm the POCs.
[05:29] Meera Patel: we'll confirm the POC list this week.
[05:32] Lina Ortega: ok next steps recap, I'll read them out and we'll confirm on the recording: 1) Lina to send joint co-sell playbook + 1-pager (by 1/14). 2) Marcus to send benchmark plan + propose 2 dates for a 90-min session (by 1/18). 3) Priya to draft partner comp and invoicing flow (by 1/17). 4) StratusWorks to share top 25 target accounts + ICP scoring and POC contact list (by 1/20). 5) Tom to provide sanitized sample logs for compliance check (by 1/16).
[05:58] Tom Novak: noted, I'll pull those logs and strip PII. small ask: can we do the Dedicated trial in us-east for network proximity to our customers?
[06:06] Marcus Chen: yes we can provision in us-east region. we'll include latency tests to external endpoints.
[06:12] Aisha Rahman: any blockers from legal for a co-sell contract template?
[06:16] Priya Nair: we'll share a standard partner addendum; legal may ask for data processing addenda and standard confidentiality clauses — nothing out of the ordinary.
[06:27] Dave Hersch: ok good. one last thing — pricing carve. we'll need to present a simple per-seat or per-conversation illustration for sales decks.
[06:33] Lina Ortega: we'll create a slide showing token-cost scenarios and a suggested resale margin so field can price simply.
[06:39] Meera Patel: thanks. that's it from our side.
[06:42] Lina Ortega: thanks all, we'll follow up in email and drop the playbook + security pack.
[06:46] Dave Hersch: thanks, bye.

End of transcript.

Notes: occasional transcription glitches around model quantization shorthand ("q8" transcribed as "q ate") and product names; speaker overlap brief at 03:42. References to shared artifacts: joint_playbook_draft_v1.docx (to be shared), redwood_security_pack_v2.pdf (to be shared), benchmark_matrix_template.csv (to be shared).
